slides.title: Marketing Mix
slides.text:
Marketing Mix
Introduced by Jerome McCarthy in 1960’s
Set of controllable variables to meet the needs of the target customers
Toolkit to achieve the marketing objective.
4 P’s of Marketing- Product, Price, Place, Promotion

bullets.text: Introduced by Jerome McCarthy in 1960’s

Toolkit to achieve the marketing objective.

slides.visual_text: Heading: Marketing Mix. Left: the four bullets in the slide text (introduced by Jerome McCarthy in 1960's; set of controllable variables to meet the needs of the target customers; toolkit to achieve the marketing objective; 4 P's of Marketing: Product, Price, Place, Promotion). Right: a tree diagram with Marketing mix at the top and arrows to four lists. Product: Product variety, Quality, Design, Features, Brand name, Packaging, Sizes, Services, Warranties, Returns. Price: List price, Discounts, Allowances, Payment period, Credit terms. Promotion: Sales promotion, Advertising, Sales force, Public relations, Direct marketing. Place: Channels, Coverage, Assortments, Locations, Inventory, Transport.

slides.title: Marketing Environment
slides.text:
Marketing Environment
A company’s marketing environment consists of the actors and forces outside of marketing that affect marketing management ability to build and maintain successful relationships with target customers.

bullets.text: A company’s marketing environment consists of the actors and forces outside of marketing that affect marketing management ability to build and maintain successful relationships with target customers.

slides.visual_text: Text only: the heading Marketing Environment and the one-sentence definition in the slide text.

slides.text:
Micro environment
It consists of the actors close to the company that directly affects its ability to serve its customers.

bullets.text: Micro environment
It consists of the actors close to the company that directly affects its ability to serve its customers.

slides.visual_text: Heading: Micro environment, with the definition in the slide text. Below it a half-circle diagram with Marketing at the centre and two-way arrows to six outer segments, from left to right: The company, Suppliers, Marketing intermediaries, Customers, Competitors, Publics.

slides.title: The Company
slides.text:
The Company
Groups such as top management, finance, research and development (R&D), purchasing, operations, and accounting.
Internal departments have an impact on the marketing department’s plans and actions.
Suppliers
Suppliers form an important link in the company’s overall customer value delivery network.
They provide the resources needed by the company to produce its goods and services.
Supply shortages or delays, labor strikes, and other events.

slides.title: Marketing Intermediaries
slides.text:
Marketing Intermediaries
Firms that help the company to promote, sell, and distribute its goods to final buyers.
Include retailers, logistics firms, marketing services agencies, and financial intermediaries

slides.title: Competitors
slides.text:
Competitors
A company must provide greater customer value and satisfaction than its competitors do.
Public
Any group that has an actual or potential interest in or impact on an organization’s ability to achieve its objectives.
Media, Local Public, Labor Union, consumer organizations, Environmental groups
Customers

Macro environment
It consists of larger societal forces existing outside the organization that affects the organization

slides.title: The Demographic Environment
slides.text:
The Demographic Environment
Demography is the study of human populations in terms of size, density, location, age, gender, diversity, race, occupation, and other statistics.

bullets.text: Demography is the study of human populations in terms of size, density, location, age, gender, diversity, race, occupation, and other statistics.

slides.visual_text: Heading The Demographic Environment with the definition in the slide text. Two photos. Left: a skier racing down a snowy slope seated on a ski frame, holding short poles with small skis on the ends. Right: a tall blue sign printed IKEA in yellow letters on a pole, beside a large blue and yellow store building with a big car park.

slides.title: The Economic Environment
slides.text:
The Economic Environment
Markets require buying power as well as people. The economic environment consists of economic factors that affect consumer purchasing power and spending patterns.
Example: inflation, interest rates, employment, GDP
Changes in Consumer Spending.

bullets.text: Markets require buying power as well as people. The economic environment consists of economic factors that affect consumer purchasing power and spending patterns.
Example: inflation, interest rates, employment, GDP
Changes in Consumer Spending.

slides.visual_text: Heading The Economic Environment with the slide text. Right: a print ad. Large handwritten headline: now you can. Smaller handwritten lines (small but readable): Can you imagine a car within the reach of all? Can you fit your family into the smallest of cars? Without a squeeze? Can you feel the safety of a big car? In a car nearly half its size? Can you find more miles in your every litre? Almost as much as a two wheeler? Can you make a difference to the environment? By hurting it the least? Can you imagine a car that will change the world? Again. A small yellow car sits on a splash of blue and purple paint, with nano on its number plate. Printed words: TATA at the top right, nano at the bottom right, TATA MOTORS at the bottom left.

slides.title: The Natural Environment
slides.text:
The Natural Environment
The natural environment involves the natural resources that are needed as inputs by marketers or that are affected by marketing activities.

bullets.text: The natural environment involves the natural resources that are needed as inputs by marketers or that are affected by marketing activities.

slides.visual_text: Heading The Natural Environment with the definition in the slide text. Two photos. Left: a pile of cardboard delivery boxes printed amazon, left at a front door. Right: a man standing in a bright living room beside a tall silver appliance with an open loop on top, with red lines drawn streaming out of it across the room. No name is printed on the appliance.

slides.text:
The Political and Legal Environment
The political environment consists of laws, change in government agencies, and
pressure groups that influence or limit various organizations and individuals in a
given society.
The Cultural Environment
Society’s basic values, perceptions, preferences, norms and behaviors

bullets.text: Internal
External

slides.visual_text: A two by two SWOT grid. Row labels on the left: Internal (top row) and External (bottom row). Column labels at the bottom: Positive (left) and Negative (right). Strengths: Internal capabilities that may help the company reach its objectives. Weaknesses: Internal limitations that may interfere with the company's ability to achieve its objectives. Opportunities: External factors that the company may be able to exploit to its advantage. Threats: Current and emerging external factors that may challenge the company's performance.
